knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The test checks compatibility with the sanded timber and any remaining finish, and shows the likely result.
Thin coats applied as the label states are the safer approach. Thick coats can trap solvent and show marks.
Access is restricted until the stated cure time has passed. A floor that feels dry can still be soft underneath.
The walkthrough checks the floor against the acceptance criteria and records remaining defects and what is agreed.
The signed handover record is evidence of what was agreed. It is not a guarantee of how the floor will look later.

practicalCriteria: Candidate confirms a finish against the scope and records the product, batch and SDS.
Candidate tests the finish on an offcut, records the result and obtains client acceptance before the whole floor is finished.
Candidate applies a thin coat to a sample area as the label states, and records the time of the coat and the recoat time.
Candidate walks a sample floor under raking light against the acceptance criteria and records any remaining defect and the handover.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Finish record with product, batch, coats and times
Offcut test record with client acceptance
Handover record signed by the client or the assessor-observed walkthrough
stopWorkCriteria: Whole floor finished before the test is accepted
Foot traffic allowed before the stated cure time
Finish applied without a compatibility check over an existing finish
